resume: Full copy or extract, with or without parentage: who can request it, how to get it free of charge at the town hall, by post or online, and what to do if a certificate drawn up in Mayotte contains an error.
aQuoiCaSert: The birth certificate (acte de naissance) proves your child's identity and parentage (filiation). You are often asked for it for a first ID card or passport, court proceedings or some registrations. The request is always free. For a birth in Mayotte, the certificate is issued by the town hall (mairie) of the town of birth.
quiEstConcerne: Parents who need their minor child's birth certificate (they are the child's legal representatives).
Anyone who needs their own birth certificate, or that of an ancestor, a descendant, their spouse or PACS partner (civil partnership).
aSavoir: There are three formats. Full copy (copie intégrale): the whole certificate, with the parents and the notes in the margin. Extract with parentage (extrait avec filiation): a summary including the parents. Extract without parentage (extrait sans filiation): identity, date and place of birth only.

Full copy and extract with parentage: reserved for the person concerned or their legal representative, their spouse or PACS partner, their ancestors and descendants, and certain professionals. Anyone can request the extract without parentage.
The request is free: never pay a private website to get a birth certificate.
In person, at the town hall of the place of birth, the certificate is handed over immediately on presentation of ID.
French child or parent born abroad: the certificate is issued by the Service central d'état civil (Scec, the central civil registry office) in Nantes, online or by post only.
Separated parents: each parent can request a full copy of their child's certificate on their own, without the other parent's agreement.

Mayotte's civil registry review commission (commission de révision de l'état civil), responsible for reconstructing old records, has not been active since around 2011. An error in a certificate is now corrected through the civil registrar (officier d'état civil) or the public prosecutor (procureur de la République).

documents.libelle: The exact details of the birth
documents.detail: Child's surname, first names, date and place of birth, surnames and first names of both parents. Copy them from the family record book (livret de famille).
Required at the town hall desk.
Useful to prove your link with the child.

documents.libelle: Full copy of the birth certificate received
documents.detail: Note the date of issue: many procedures require a certificate less than 3 months old.

etapes.titre: Check whether you really need it
etapes.detail: Ask the organization which format it wants (usually the full copy) and whether it must be less than 3 months old.

etapes.titre: Go to or write to the town hall of the place of birth
etapes.detail: By post on plain paper: type of certificate wanted, surname, first names, date of birth, parents' names, your link with the child and your address.
On service-public.gouv.fr, free service "Demande d'acte de naissance", if the town of birth is offered there.

etapes.titre: Check before going to the town hall
etapes.detail: The right town hall (the one in the place of birth), original ID, family record book, exact names of both parents, type of certificate wanted.

etapes.titre: Born abroad: go through the Scec in Nantes
etapes.detail: Apply online on service-public.gouv.fr or by post to the Service central d'état civil, 11 rue de la Maison Blanche, 44941 Nantes Cedex 09.
Scan it into the Vault and note its date.

ou.nom: Town hall of the place of birth, civil registry office (état civil)
ou.detail: Issued immediately at the desk, on presentation of ID.
Free, for a birth in France if the town is connected.
For French people born abroad. Online or by post.
